criterion_scores.reasoning: The main nominal behavior is sound: it reads Stop-hook JSON, extracts session_id, builds a content-gated build_session record, appends JSONL, and conditionally projects to PostHog only when POSTHOG_PROJECT_KEY is set. The emitted record avoids transcript body content and uses jq JSON construction. However, line 44 can produce false negatives for build_dir_touched by ignoring MultiEdit/Bash modification paths and limiting detection to Edit/Write. The unchecked append also weakens the 'always append authoritative record' behavior under failure conditions, though the nominal path works.

Most expected pieces are present: disable override, transcript metrics, optional semantic metadata, authoritative JSONL output, and optional PostHog projection. The main incompleteness is coverage of build touches: line 44 only covers a subset of write mechanisms and .claude subdirectories, so some build artifact edits will not be represented. No missing deterministic references were supplied.

The artifact follows the expected hook shape: project-relative .claude paths, local settings opt-out, silent success, append-only artifact output, and environment-gated external projection. I did not see violations of the supplied house constraints such as MCP write misuse, project-skill naming, or tombstoned measurement-store choices. I am not assigning 1.0 because the full repository hook convention/frontmatter expectations are not supplied beyond this file and comments.

The implementation is lean and contract-first: JSONL source of truth plus a swappable PostHog projection, no collector/platform overbuild, no hardcoded secret, and no duplicated measurement store. The Langfuse mention is explicitly about deferring that platform, not resurrecting it. Minor concern remains that silent telemetry drops can create misleading metrics, but the design avoids the major listed anti-patterns.

The script is readable and sectioned, and optional PostHog failures are reasonably non-blocking. But load-bearing telemetry-loss paths are too quiet: line 82 does not check whether the authoritative append succeeded, and line 76 suppresses record-construction errors with exit 0. Given the comments distinguish silent success, failures should be more explicable than they are here.

defects.quote: if jq -es 'any(.[]?; (.message.content // []) | .[]? | select(.type=="tool_use" and (.name=="Edit" or .name=="Write")) | ((.input.file_path // "") | test("\\.claude/(skills|agents|commands|hooks)")))' "$TRANSCRIPT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
defects.description: The build_dir_touched metric only recognizes Edit and Write tool calls into four .claude subdirectories. It misses common modification paths such as MultiEdit and Bash-created/modified files, so sessions that did touch build artifacts can be recorded as build_dir_touched=false.

defects.description: The build touch detector covers skills, agents, commands, and hooks but not other build artifact areas referenced by the broader build-quality scope, such as reference docs. If this telemetry is meant to represent build-session activity generally, this leaves a secondary but real coverage gap.

defects.spec_ref: Contract comment lines 5-6: ALWAYS append an authoritative build_session record to .claude/artifacts/build-sessions.jsonl
defects.description: The authoritative append is not checked. Because the script does not use set -e and does not test this command's status, permission/disk/path failures can be silently ignored while the hook still exits 0, leaving no systemMessage or other diagnostic despite losing the source-of-truth record.

Record-construction failures are suppressed and converted to a successful no-op. That is defensible for a non-blocking hook, but it makes telemetry loss hard to explain when jq input or environment assumptions are wrong.
